arxiv-1801-03535.title: Measurement of the \PZ / γ ∗ → τ ​ τ \PZ/\gamma^{*}\to\tau\tau cross section in pp collisions at s = \sqrt{s}= 13 \TeV and validation of τ \tau lepton analysis techniques
arxiv-1801-03535.description: Abstract A measurement is presented of the \PZ / γ ∗ → τ ​ τ \PZ/\gamma^{*}\to\tau\tau cross section in pp collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV , using data recorded by the CMS experiment at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 2.3 \fbinv .

arxiv-2204-02952.title: Inducing Positive Perspectives with Text Reframing
arxiv-2204-02952.creator: Caleb Ziems ⋆ † Minzhi Li ⋆ ⋄ Anthony Zhang † Diyi Yang †
arxiv-2204-02952.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Caleb Ziems ⋆ † Minzhi Li ⋆ ⋄ Anthony Zhang † Diyi Yang †. Sentiment transfer is one popular example of a text style transfer task, where the goal is to reverse the sentiment polarity of a text. With a sentiment reversal comes also a reversal in meaning. We introduce a different but related task called positive reframing in which we neutralize a negative point of view and generate a more positive perspective for the author without contradicting the original meaning.

arxiv-2305-15079.title: Life cycle economic viability analysis of battery storage in electricity market
arxiv-2305-15079.creator: Yinguo Yang, Yiling Ye, Zhuoxiao Cheng, Guangchun Ruan, Qiuyu Lu, Xuan Wang, Haiwang Zhong
arxiv-2305-15079.description: Abstract Battery storage is essential to enhance the flexibility and reliability of electric power systems by providing auxiliary services and load shifting. Storage owners typically gains incentives from quick responses to auxiliary service prices, but frequent charging and discharging also reduce its lifetime.

arxiv-2308-11580.title: Discontinuous Galerkin schemes for master equations modeling open quantum systems Thanks: Supported by The University of Texas at San Antonio (UTSA).
arxiv-2308-11580.creator: José A. Morales Escalante
arxiv-2308-11580.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by José A. Morales Escalante. This work presents a numerical analysis of a Discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method for a transformed master equation modeling an open quantum system: a quantum sub-system interacting with a noisy environment . It is shown that the presented transformed master equation has a reduced computational cost in comparison to a Wigner-Fokker-Planck model of the same system for the general case of non-harmonic potentials via DG schemes.

arxiv-2312-07766.title: The Central Kinematics and Black Hole Mass of 4C+37.11
arxiv-2312-07766.creator: Tirth Surti, Roger W. Romani, Julia Scharwächter, Alison Peck, Greg B. Taylor
arxiv-2312-07766.description: Abstract We report on IFU measurements of the host of the radio source 4C+37.11. This massive elliptical contains the only resolved double compact nucleus at pc-scale separation, likely a bound supermassive black hole binary (SMBHB). i i -band photometry and GMOS-N IFU spectroscopy show that the galaxy has a large r b = 1.5 ′′ r_{b}=1.

arxiv-2407-17469.title: I Could’ve Asked That : Reformulating Unanswerable Questions
arxiv-2407-17469.creator: Wenting Zhao, Ge Gao, Claire Cardie, Alexander M. Rush
arxiv-2407-17469.description: Abstract When seeking information from unfamiliar documents, users frequently pose questions that cannot be answered by the documents. While existing large language models (LLMs) identify these unanswerable questions, they do not assist users in reformulating their questions, thereby reducing their overall utility.

arxiv-2411-10894.title: Deep BI-RADS Network for Improved Cancer Detection from Mammograms
arxiv-2411-10894.creator: Gil Ben-Artzi, Feras Daragma, Shahar Mahpod
arxiv-2411-10894.description: Abstract While state-of-the-art models for breast cancer detection leverage multi-view mammograms for enhanced diagnostic accuracy, they often focus solely on visual mammography data. However, radiologists document valuable lesion descriptors that contain additional information that can enhance mammography-based breast cancer screening. A key question is whether deep learning models can benefit from these expert-derived features.

arxiv-2501-03900.creator: Gabriel Corrigan

The virtual cohomological dimension of Out ⁡ ( F n ) \operatorname{Out}(F_{n}) is given precisely by the dimension of the spine of Culler–Vogtmann Outer space. arxiv-2509-06349.title: Tunable topology, Hall response, and spin-textures in bicircularly polarized light illuminated altermagnets
arxiv-2509-06349.creator: Maitri Ganguli, Aneek Jana, Awadhesh Narayan
arxiv-2509-06349.description: Abstract Altermagnets, featuring non-relativistic spin splitting, have drawn enormous attention due to their intriguing properties. Here, we investigate the effects of shining bicircularly polarized light (BCL) on altermagnets with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We discover a remarkable tunability of topology, spin-textures, and Fermi surfaces of altermagnets by means of BCL illumination, going beyond monochromatic light.

arxiv-2511-10280.title: Scattering Gravitons off General Spinning Compact Objects to 𝒪 ⁡ ( G 2 ​ S 4 ) \mathcal{O}(G^{2}S^{4})
arxiv-2511-10280.creator: Dogan Akpinar
arxiv-2511-10280.description: Abstract We compute the classical one-loop gravitational Compton amplitude describing the scattering of a graviton off a massive spinning compact object at the second post-Minkowskian order, including terms through the quartic order in spin. Our analysis includes spin-induced finite-size effects up to the hexadecapolar order, and extends recent results obtained for minimal couplings at the quadratic order in spin.

pmc-10694928.description: BackgroundTuberculosis is one of the most serious challenges facing the global healthcare system. This study aims to investigate the incidence and mortality of tuberculosis in Iran from 2010 to 2019 as well as its relationship with the human development index (HDI).

pmc-11322606.title: TFEB activation hallmarks antigenic experience of B lymphocytes and directs germinal center fate decisions
pmc-11322606.creator: Matthias Münchhalfen, Richard Görg, Michael Haberl, Jens Löber, Jakob Willenbrink, Laura Schwarzt, Charlotte Höltermann, Christian Ickes, Leonard Hammermann, Jan Kus, Björn Chapuy, Andrea Ballabio, Sybille D Reichardt, Alexander Flügel, Niklas Engels, Jürgen Wienands
pmc-11322606.description: Ligation of the B cell antigen receptor (BCR) initiates humoral immunity. However, BCR signaling without appropriate co-stimulation commits B cells to death rather than to differentiation into immune effector cells. How BCR activation depletes potentially autoreactive B cells while simultaneously primes for receiving rescue and differentiation signals from cognate T lymphocytes remains unknown.

pmc-11431625.title: Survival Trends for Uterine Sarcomas from a Tertiary Center: The Oxford Experience
pmc-11431625.creator: Aakriti Aggarwal, Federico Ferrari, Andreas Zouridis, Sean Kehoe, Sarah Pratap, Elisa Gozzini, Hooman Soleymani Majd, Julio Plaza-Díaz
pmc-11431625.description: Simple SummaryWe analyzed the clinicopathological characteristics, management, and survival trends in women diagnosed with uterine sarcoma at our tertiary institute over ten years. We studied the recurrence trends and their management, with a further focus on patterns of the follow-up. This study generates meaningful real-world data to help offer more insight into these rare gynecological cancers.

pmc-11532072.title: Development of novel CDK9 and CYP3A4 inhibitors for cancer therapy through field and computational approaches
pmc-11532072.creator: Aisha A. Alsfouk, Abdelmoujoud Faris, Ivana Cacciatore, Radwan Alnajjar
pmc-11532072.description: Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9) and cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) have emerged as promising targets in the development of anticancer drugs, presenting a consistent challenge in the quest for potent inhibitors. CDK9 inhibitors can selectively target fast-growing cancer cells by disrupting transcription elongation, which in turn hinders the production of proteins essential for cell cycle progression and survivaŚ.

pmc-11589386.title: Preferences of people living with HIV for features of tuberculosis preventive treatment regimens in Uganda: a discrete choice experiment
pmc-11589386.creator: Hélène E Aschmann, Allan Musinguzi, Jillian L Kadota, Catherine Namale, Juliet Kakeeto, Jane Nakimuli, Lydia Akello, Fred Welishe, Anne Nakitende, Christopher Berger, David W Dowdy, Adithya Cattamanchi, Fred C Semitala, Andrew D Kerkhoff
pmc-11589386.description: IntroductionTuberculosis (TB) preventive treatment (TPT) is recommended for people living with HIV (PLHIV) in high TB burden settings. While 6 months of daily isoniazid remains widely used, shorter regimens are now available. However, little is known about preferences of PLHIV for key features of TPT regimens.

pmc-12639776.title: Cellular hnRNP AB inhibits avian influenza virus RNA synthesis via blocking UAP56-mediated nuclear export of PB2 mRNA
pmc-12639776.creator: Shuhui Liu, Yue Sun, Yunling Peng, Chenchen Xu, Suquan Song, Liping Yan
pmc-12639776.description: Avian influenza viral ribonucleoproteins (vRNPs) complete genome transcription and replication by interacting with host proteins, and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is its major component. PB2 is a component of RdRp and plays an important role in viral RNA synthesis. Our previous mass spectrometry analysis identified PB2 interacted with avian cellular heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein AB (hnRNP AB).

pmc-12877273.title: Comfort feeding in hospitalised people with dementia: a retrospective study of survival following comfort feeding recommendations
pmc-12877273.creator: Christine Davis, Nasime Mokari-Manshadi, Viviane De Menezes Caceres, Patrick Russell, Toby Gilbert, Stephen Hedger, Udul Hewage, Dirk Hoffman, Yogesh Sharma, Alice O’Connell, Amrit Sandhu, Jeff Faunt, Campbell Thompson
pmc-12877273.description: ObjectivesPersistent and significant swallowing impairment can occur in individuals with dementia. Determining prognosis and establishing realistic goals of care in this population is complex and comfort feeding may be recommended. This study aimed to establish evidence relating to patient outcomes following recommendation of comfort feeding to aid informed decision making.

pmc-13024148.title: An In Vitro Study on the Efficacy of Green Synthesized Silver Nanoparticles on Surgical Site Infections and Healings
pmc-13024148.creator: Gürkan Güneri, Merve Keskin
pmc-13024148.description: Background/Objectives: The healing rate of wounds resulting from postoperative abdominal surgery interventions increases as the inflammation and infections in the wound are reduced. However, antibiotic resistance among microorganisms increases the incidence of surgical site infections (SSIs). Therefore, the need for new products that exhibit antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities, in addition to antibiotics, is increasing.

pmc-13096444.title: Water quality index and human health risk analysis in urban drinking water sources
pmc-13096444.creator: Iqra Nasim, Rab Nawaz, Aysha Farwa, Sajjad Ahmad, Muhammad Atif Irshad, Sami A Al-Hussain, Ali Irfan, Magdi E A Zaki
pmc-13096444.description: The present study was conducted to assess the quality of drinking water in urban areas of Hafizabad and Pindi Bhattian through the Water Quality Index (WQI) and Human Health Risk Assessment (HHRA). Forty-eight samples were collected from four sources of drinking water, including filter plants, tube wells, tap water, and bore wells.

pmc-13450532.title: Muscle in fat trouble: The rise of IMAT in metabolic and musculoskeletal disease
pmc-13450532.creator: Vanessa M. Weik, Andreas L. Birkenfeld, Andreas Peter, Cora Weigert, Simon I. Dreher
pmc-13450532.description: Intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) is increasingly recognized as a contributor to insulin resistance and metabolic dysfunction in type 2 diabetes (T2D). Accumulation of IMAT was found to correlate with impaired skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity, as well as a generally reduced muscle strength and physical performance in humans.

uslaw-usc-t33-s661.title: 33 U.S.C. § 661 — Creation of commission; appointment of members; vacancies; powers generally
uslaw-usc-t33-s661.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t33-s661.description: United States Code, Title 33 (Navigation And Navigable Waters); Chapter 14 (California Debris Commission). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. A commission is created, to be known as the California Debris Commission, consisting of three members. The President of the United States shall, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, appoint the commission from officers of the Corps of Engineers.
